sections.text:
1 Al-Mahdi mortuus est die 4 Augusti a. 785 p. C.; cf. Weil, Gesch. der Cha-
lifen (1848), t. II, p. 113. — Assemani, Bibl. Orient., III, 1, p. 161 a, dixit Chaliphae
Rashidi temporibus claruisse Theophilum astronomum, teste Amro. Sed mirum
in modum erravit, nam Amrus de Theophilo quodam Edesseno, aerarii praefecto
non de astronomo loquitur; cf. Gismondi, Maris Amri et Slibae de patr. Nesto-
rian., Romae, 1899, I, p. 66. — De alio Theophilo Edesseno qui saeculo V, ut
videtur, vitas martyrum syriace scripsit, cf. Byzant. Zeitschr., IX, p. 580; XI,
p. 241.
2 Ibn el Qifṭî († 1248 p. C.) in libro de vitis virorum doctorum (Târîch el
ḥokama). Germanicam versionem capituli de Theophilo liberalissime mecum
communicavit Carolus Dyroff ex codice Monacensi Arab. 440, f. 44v : “ Theophil,
Sohn des Thomas, der Astronom, aus Edessa. Dieser Astronom lebte in Bagdad
und war das Haupt der Astronomen des Al-Mâhdi. Er war kundig in den
Geschichten (?) der Sterne und hat in der ” astronomia iudiciaria „ merkwürdige
Fälle vom Eintreffen (seiner Voraussagungen) gehabt, noch als er sich bereits
seinem 90 Lebensjahr näherte. „
3 Albohazen Haly filius Abenragel, In iudiciis stellarum ed. impensis Io. Ba. Sessa,
1503, vide e. g., p. 11 : Dixit Nayfel filius Thome... (lege “ Ṭâ’ûfîl „ i. e. Theophi-
lus) et p. 25 : Quando a te quaesitum fuerit pro aliqua civitate vel castro si
obsidebitur vel non; aut, si obsidebitur, si capietur vel non, et si capietur, si pro
pace aut violentia. Cf. cod. Paris. 2417, f. 23 : Ἐὰν ἐρωτηθῇς περὶ πόλεως πολιορ-
κεῖται ἢ οὔ καὶ ἐὰν πολιορκῆται, σώζεται ἢ παραλαμβάνεται ... et supra p. 68,
capp. κζ', κθ'.
4 Cf. Steinschneider, Hebräische Uebersetz. des Mittelalters, p. 833, n. 372.
5 De Theophili excerptis in “ Syntagmate Laurentiano „ saec. IX, cf. Boll, Sitzb.
Akad. Münch., 1899, p. 92 ss.; in “ Syntagmate Parisino „ saec. XI, cf. Catal., II,
p. 37, n. 1 et p. 35, f. 203 ss. In omnibus fere codicibus capitulum quoddam huius
astrologi inveneris.
6 Catal., I, p. 129 : Περὶ κοσμικῶν καταρχῶν; Catal., II, p. 195 : Περὶ ζωῆς;
Catal., IV, p, 93 : Περὶ προβολῆς ἄρχοντος; p. 122 (= Ludwich, Maximi reliq.,

sections.en:
1 Al-Mahdi died on the 4th day of August in the year 785 A.D.; cf. Weil, Gesch. der Cha-
lifen (1848), vol. II, p. 113. — Assemani, Bibl. Orient., III, 1, p. 161 a, said that in the times of the Caliph
Rashid the astronomer Theophilus flourished, on the testimony of Amrus. But he erred in a wondrous
manner, for Amrus speaks of a certain Theophilus of Edessa, a prefect of the treasury,
not of an astronomer; cf. Gismondi, Maris Amri et Slibae de patr. Nesto-
rian., Rome, 1899, I, p. 66. — Concerning another Theophilus of Edessa who in the 5th century, as
it seems, wrote the lives of the martyrs in Syriac, cf. Byzant. Zeitschr., IX, p. 580; XI,
p. 241.
2 Ibn el Qifṭî († 1248 A.D.) in the book on the lives of learned men (Târîch el
ḥokama). The German version of the chapter on Theophilus was most liberally communicated to me
by Karl Dyroff from the Munich Arabic codex 440, f. 44v : “ Theophilus,
son of Thomas, the astronomer, from Edessa. This astronomer lived in Baghdad
and was the head of the astronomers of Al-Mâhdi. He was knowledgeable in the
histories (?) of the stars and in ” astronomia iudiciaria „ had remarkable
cases of the fulfillment (of his predictions), even when he was already
approaching his 90th year of life. „
3 Albohazen Haly son of Abenragel, In iudiciis stellarum published at the expense of Io. Ba. Sessa,
1503, see e. g., p. 11 : Nayfel son of Thomas said... (read “ Ṭâ’ûfîl „ i. e. Theophi-
lus) and p. 25 : When it shall have been asked of you concerning any city or fort whether
it will be besieged or not; or, if it will be besieged, whether it will be taken or not, and if it will be taken, whether by
peace or violence. Cf. Paris codex 2417, f. 23 : Ἐὰν ἐρωτηθῇς περὶ πόλεως πολιορ-
κεῖται ἢ οὔ καὶ ἐὰν πολιορκῆται, σώζεται ἢ παραλαμβάνεται ... ('If you are asked concerning a city whether it is besieged
or not and if it is besieged, whether it is saved or taken ...') and above p. 68,
chaps. 27, 29.
4 Cf. Steinschneider, Hebräische Uebersetz. des Mittelalters, p. 833, n. 372.
5 Concerning the excerpts of Theophilus in the “ Syntagma Laurentianum „ of the 9th cent., cf. Boll, Sitzb.
Akad. Münch., 1899, p. 92 ff.; in the “ Syntagma Parisinum „ of the 11th cent., cf. Catal., II,
p. 37, n. 1 and p. 35, f. 203 ff. In almost all codices you will find a certain chapter of this
astrologer.
6 Catal., I, p. 129 : Περὶ κοσμικῶν καταρχῶν ('On cosmic inceptions'); Catal., II, p. 195 : Περὶ ζωῆς ('On life');
Catal., IV, p, 93 : Περὶ προβολῆς ἄρχοντος ('On the projection of a ruler'); p. 122 (= Ludwich, Maximi reliq.,
p. 120) : on plants and animals pertaining to the planets; above p. 212; On the fixed stars,
cf.

summary.headline: Theophilus and Byzantine Astrological Collections
summary.text: Discussion of Theophilus of Edessa: his books in the secret palace library at Baghdad, his influence on Abu Maʿshar and Abenragel, and the transmission of his astrological chapters through Greek and Byzantine collections from the ninth to eleventh centuries. Notes cite Ibn al-Qifṭī, Albohazen Haly, the Syntagma Laurentianum and Syntagma Parisinum, and topics including cosmic inceptions, life, planetary plants and animals, and fixed stars.
